name: Hamish Yeo
life: “I still remember paying a writer's light bill with my winter bonus.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Hamish by a small Sunday habit. Hamish pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I paid the electricity through a lean winter. My price was one honest conversation after the launch.
appearance: Hamish is easy to recognize by a blunt cut just below the ears and a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Usually dressed in a faded indigo overshirt with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve, Hamish looks down for a moment before saying something difficult when listening.
personality: Hamish loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Hamish remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To have one honest post-launch conversation.
family: Eric Hassan is Hamish’s stepsibling. Hamish is free to hang up first. Eric makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Low water music*, Eric says, “I thought the sound came from the old fog bell.”
connections: Jacqueline Glass. One supporter paid to keep the lights on while another kept the writer's own voice audible.
